1. First: `data = data.join(name_count, on ="RescuerID")` - this adds a column called "name_count"
2. Second: `data = data.join(name_count, on="Name")` - this also tries to add a column called "name_count", which already exists

The second join is trying to add "name_count" again, but the column already exists from the first join. This causes the "columns overlap" error.

I see now that the function needs to correctly join the name counts. The first join is definitely incorrect, mistakenly using "RescuerID" instead of "Name". The second join correctly uses "Name" to match name counts. Removing the first problematic line should resolve the join conflict and ensure accurate name count tracking.
